name: Split Step
summary: The split step is a small hop you make just before your opponent hits the ball, landing on the balls of both feet at the moment of their contact. It puts you in a position to push off in any direction instead of being caught mid-stride. Every strong player does it on nearly every shot, and most players below 3.5 do not do it at all.
whenToUse: Every time an opponent is about to make contact. This is a habit, not a situational choice.
You are walking forward behind a drop or a return and they are about to hit.
You are at the kitchen line and a speed-up could come at any moment.
You have just hit a ball and your feet want to keep travelling.
howTo: Watch your opponent's paddle as they start their swing, not the ball.
Hop just enough to unweight both feet — an inch or two off the ground, not a jump.
Time the landing so both feet touch down as their paddle meets the ball.
Land about shoulder width apart, on the balls of your feet, with soft knees.
Push off the foot furthest from the ball and move.
commonMistakes: Landing after they hit rather than as they hit, which leaves you in the air at the moment you need to push off.
Hopping too high, so you are still coming down when the ball is already past you.
Landing flat-footed or on your heels, which kills the push-off you split-stepped for.
Skipping it while running forward through the transition zone — that is exactly when you need it.
Landing with your feet together, which leaves you with no base to push against.

drills.name: Split on their contact
drills.description: Your partner feeds from the other side of the net. You do nothing but split-step on each feed and freeze — no swing. The point is to separate the timing from the shot so you can feel when you are late.

drills.name: Split and go
drills.description: Same feed, but now your partner sends the ball to a random side without telling you. Split as they contact, push off, and touch the ball with your paddle. You are training the push-off, not the shot.

drills.name: Ladder of hops
drills.description: No ball. Stand at the kitchen line and split-step once every three seconds, checking each landing: shoulder width, balls of the feet, knees bent, paddle up. Quiet feet mean you are landing softly enough to move.
